kf: Sort blisters by **level of split**: intraepidermal (flaccid, erosions: pemphigus, impetigo, SSSS, SJS/TEN) vs subepidermal (tense: pemphigoid, DH, PCT, EBA).
Ask: age, acute or chronic, mucosa, itch vs pain, drugs, sites, systemic illness.
Emergencies: **SJS/TEN, SSSS, extensive pemphigus, eczema herpeticum, neonatal blistering**.
Investigations: swab (bacteria, HSV PCR), skin biopsy of a fresh blister edge plus perilesional skin for **direct immunofluorescence**, serology.
Common causes in primary care: impetigo, insect bites, friction, contact dermatitis, pompholyx, herpes.
myths: **"Blisters are always infection"**: autoimmune and drug causes need biopsy and urgent referral.
patho_lead: Where the skin **splits** decides how a blister looks.

mech.t: Fragile roof breaks easily: erosions and crusts (bullous impetigo, pemphigus foliaceus).
Desmosome loss in pemphigus vulgaris: flaccid blisters, mucosal erosions.
Basement membrane damage (pemphigoid, DH, PCT, EBA): tense blisters.
SJS/TEN: the whole epidermis dies and sloughs.

comp: Infection, fluid loss, scarring, mucosal strictures.
